questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Latvia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Latvia article.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Latvia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Latvia article.

questions.proof: They speak the Latvian language, which is a little like the Lithuanian language but is not close enough to be understood.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Latvia's neighbours to the east are the countries _____ and Belarus.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “countries”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Latvia article.

questions.proof: Latvia's neighbours to the east are the countries Russia and Belarus.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is one of the Baltic states, together with _____ in the north and Lithuania in the south.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “together”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Latvia article.

questions.proof: It is one of the Baltic states, together with Estonia in the north and Lithuania in the south.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was briefly under German occupation during World War II in from _____ to 1944.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Latvia article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: It was briefly under German occupation during World War II in from 1941 to 1944.
